summary: This benchmark evaluates whether an attention edge identified by an edit-sensitive hidden-state displacement statistic on a calibration set is sufficient or necessary to propagate a declaration edit in Qwen2.5-14B. Testing on 384 held-out pairs reveals a decisive negative result: opening block 20 alone achieves 0 of 384 reversals, while leaving block 20 closed still achieves 332 reversals. The experimental design is rigorous and methodologically sound, though the scope is restricted to a single selected block.
strengths: Rigorous counterfactual experimental setup with clean separation between calibration (64 groups) and test evaluations (384 groups).
Comprehensive control baselines including unrestricted direct-read, leave-one-out, single-edge, and fully closed schedules.
Precise statistical reporting including paired 95% confidence intervals (-90.10 to -83.33 for single-block reduction; 0.00 to 0.78 for exclusion reduction) and logit margins.
Complete specification of model checkpoint commit hash, layer counts, framework versions (MLX 0.32.4, mlx-lm 0.32.2), and execution runtime.
weaknesses: No primary repository was formally linked in submission metadata (evaluated under text_only badge).

The analysis investigates only the single top-ranked block (block 20) rather than presenting a full sweep across all 48 blocks to establish how predictive hidden-state displacement is across the layer spectrum.
Brief exposition (527 words) that leaves theoretical explanations for the disconnect between displacement metrics and causal mediation unaddressed.
suggestions: Include a full block-by-block intervention plot comparing calibration displacement norm against held-out single-edge reversal success across all 48 layers.
Investigate multi-edge / joint-block ablation schedules to identify whether the mechanism exhibits redundant multi-head routing or cumulative layer effects.
Provide theoretical grounding connecting the empirical failure of single-block displacement ranking to known limitations of activation patching and local causal tracing.

claims.text: The Studio run lasted seven minutes and 26 seconds using Python 3.12, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2 and NumPy 2.5.5.
At each block from 18 to 48, hold those incoming states fixed and compute what opening the edge changes.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While ROME establishes causal tracing to locate decisiveness in mid-layer MLPs, this benchmark investigates attention-edge intervention specifically and provides concrete negative evidence that maximum hidden-state displacement in an attention layer does not imply individual necessity or sufficiency.
